v.q: Which pattern lets you swap interchangeable algorithms, such as different fee calculations, behind one interface at runtime?
v.w: Strategy encapsulates each algorithm in its own class and lets the context pick one, replacing long if/else or switch chains.

v.q: Which pattern replaces a long if/else chain that picks a discount rule by customer type?
v.w: Strategy puts each rule in its own class behind one interface, and the context picks one.

v.q: A legacy payment class has the wrong method names for your interface and you cannot change it. Which pattern fits?
v.w: Adapter wraps an incompatible class and translates calls to the interface the client expects.

v.q: Which statement about the Adapter pattern is NOT true?
o: It adds new behaviour to an object while keeping its interface
It translates calls to the interface the client expects
It helps when you cannot change the legacy class
v.w: Adding behaviour while keeping the interface is Decorator. Adapter changes the interface.

v.q: What is the Decorator pattern for?
o: Adds behaviour to an object by wrapping it, keeping the interface
Creates objects without naming their concrete class
Makes exactly one instance globally available
Defines the skeleton of an algorithm for subclasses
v.w: Java's `BufferedInputStream` wrapping `FileInputStream` is the textbook example. Spring AOP proxies work in a similar wrapping spirit.

v.q: Which Java example is a Decorator?
v.w: BufferedReader wraps another Reader and adds buffering behind the same interface.

v.q: Why is a classic hand-written Singleton often criticised?
o: It hides global state, hurts testability and needs thread-safety care
It uses far too much memory for each instance
It cannot be written in Java without reflection
It forces every class to use inheritance
v.w: In Spring, singleton scope for beans gives the one-instance benefit while dependency injection keeps code testable.

v.q: Which statement about a hand-written Singleton is NOT true?
o: A Spring singleton bean avoids its testing problems
v.w: Global state makes tests harder because the instance cannot easily be replaced with a mock.

v.q: Which pattern notifies many dependants automatically when one object changes state?
v.w: Observer decouples the subject from its listeners. Spring application events and message topics follow the same idea.

v.q: A fraud check, an email sender and an audit logger must all react when a payment is saved. Which pattern keeps the payment code unaware of them?
v.w: The subject publishes an event and listeners subscribe. Spring application events work this way.

v.q: A constructor has eight parameters, most optional. Which pattern improves readability?
v.w: Builder sets only the needed fields with named steps and then calls `build()`, avoiding telescoping constructors.

v.q: Which situation is NOT a good fit for the Builder pattern?
o: A class with two required fields and no options
A class with eight parameters, most optional
An object that is created in several steps
A request object with many optional headers
v.w: A plain constructor is clearer when there are only a few required fields.

v.q: A request must pass through validation, authentication and logging handlers, each deciding whether to continue. Which pattern is this?
v.w: Servlet filters and Spring Security's filter chain are real-world examples.

v.q: Which Java feature is NOT an example of Chain of Responsibility?
o: Log handlers passing a record along
v.w: HashMap is a data structure. Each handler in a chain decides whether to continue to the next.

v.q: What is the Template Method pattern?
o: A base class fixes the steps while subclasses override some of them
A class that creates families of related objects
An object that produces copies of itself on request
One class that hides a complex subsystem behind a simple API
v.w: The superclass controls the order and subclasses fill in the variable parts. `JdbcTemplate` uses the same principle with callbacks.

v.q: JdbcTemplate takes a callback for each row and handles connections, statements and cleanup itself. Which principle is this?
v.w: The fixed steps live in the template, and your callback fills in the variable part.
